html:
Beijing is the capital of China, on the northern edge of the North China Plain, close to the mountain passes that lead to Mongolia and Manchuria. Its name means "northern capital".

It was a frontier town for most of its early history. The northern conquest dynasties made it a capital: the Khitan Liao as a southern capital, then the Jurchen Jin from 1153. Genghis Khan's army sacked it in 1215. Kublai Khan built a new city there, Dadu, which the Turks and Mongols called Khanbaliq, as the capital of his Yuan dynasty.

The Ming first ruled from Nanjing, but the Yongle Emperor moved the capital to Beijing in 1421 and built the Forbidden City at its heart. Under the Ming and the Qing it was the seat of the emperors for almost five hundred years. The Jesuit Matteo Ricci reached it in 1601. In 1900 the Boxers besieged its foreign legations.

The Nationalists moved the capital to Nanjing in 1928, but on 1 October 1949 Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic from Tiananmen gate and made Beijing the capital again. In 1989 the army crushed the Tiananmen Square protests. It hosted the 2008 Olympics and is now a city of over 20 million.
sum: Beijing is the capital of China, on the northern edge of the North China Plain, close to the mountain passes that lead to Mongolia and Manchuria. Its name means "northern capital".
